title: Unit 1 Study Guide

assessment.name: Unit 1 assessment
assessment.format: 12 multiple-choice questions (26 minutes), then two short code tasks with supplied method headers (24 minutes).

lede: Practice the skills on the Unit 1 assessment. Practice explains each answer right away. The mock collects your answers first, like the real thing.

sections.title: How Java runs
ideas: Compile-time errors stop a program from running at all. Run-time errors crash it while it runs. Logic errors run fine but give wrong answers.
Every statement ends with a semicolon; Strings use double quotes; Java is case-sensitive.
Names use letters, digits, _ and $, cannot start with a digit, and cannot be reserved words. Classes are LikeThis; variables and methods are likeThis.
n bits can represent 2ⁿ different values. RAM is volatile: it loses its contents without power.

sections.title: Expressions and types
ideas: int / int is an int: the fraction is truncated toward zero, not rounded. % gives the remainder, with the sign of the left operand.
The right side is evaluated first; assignment happens last. A double variable does not undo integer division.
An int can be stored in a double (widening). A double needs a cast to go into an int, and the cast truncates.
Where the cast goes matters: (double) a / b divides as doubles; (double) (a / b) divides as ints first.
An int that goes past Integer.MAX_VALUE wraps around, with no error.

sections.title: Output and + with Strings
ideas: print leaves the cursor on the same line; println moves to the next line afterwards. Neither adds spaces.
\n is a new line, \t a tab, \" a quote character, and \\ a backslash.
+ works left to right. Once one side is a String, + joins text: "a" + 1 + 2 is "a12", but 1 + 2 + "a" is "3a".
* / % still happen before +, so "x" + 3 * 4 is "x12".

sections.title: String methods
ideas: Indexes start at 0 and end at length() − 1. substring(a, b) starts at a and stops before b, so its length is b − a.
substring(length()) and substring(k, k) are legal and return "". Going past length() throws an exception.
indexOf returns where the first match starts, or −1 if there is none. Case matters.
compareTo stops at the first different character and subtracts; if one String runs out first, it subtracts the lengths.
length() and indexOf return int; equals returns boolean; substring returns a new String. Strings never change.

sections.title: Math.random and method signatures
ideas: Math.random() is at least 0.0 and less than 1.0. For min to max inclusive: (int) (Math.random() * (max − min + 1)) + min.
Cast after multiplying. (int) Math.random() is always 0.
A method header tells you the argument types, in order, and the return type. An int argument can go where a double is expected, but not the reverse.
Math.abs keeps its argument's type; Math.sqrt and Math.pow always return a double.

sections.title: Objects and references
sections.source: New for the current course (the Sep 17 AliasingLab)
ideas: new creates an object and gives back a reference to it. A variable holds the reference, not the object.
b = a copies the reference: both now refer to the same object, and a change through one is seen through the other.
Reassigning a variable points it at a different object; it does not change the old one.
Calling a method on null compiles but throws a NullPointerException when it runs.
== asks "same object?"; equals asks "same contents?".

skills.errors: I can tell compile-time, run-time and logic errors apart.
skills.syntax: I can spot syntax mistakes such as a missing semicolon or a bad comment.
skills.identifiers: I can tell legal names from illegal ones and follow Java's naming conventions.
skills.bits: I can work out how many values a number of bits can represent.
skills.hardware: I can explain what RAM does and why it is volatile.
skills.division: I can predict int division, % and precedence, including negative numbers.
skills.casting: I can predict casts and say when an assignment needs one.
skills.printing: I can predict exactly what print, println and escape sequences output.
skills.concat: I can predict + with Strings, working left to right.
skills.substring: I can predict substring and length, including legal and illegal bounds.
skills.indexOf: I can use indexOf to find text and to cut a String around it.
skills.compareTo: I can compute compareTo and explain its rules.
skills.signatures: I can use a method's header to check its arguments and return type.
skills.random: I can write Math.random for any inclusive range.
skills.references: I can trace references, aliases, null, and == versus equals.

codeTasks.title: Initials
codeTasks.does: Returns the first letter of each name, each followed by a period: initials("Ada Lovelace") returns "A.L.".
codeTasks.pre: fullName contains exactly one space, which separates two non-empty names, with no spaces at the start or end.
rubric: Finds the space with indexOf instead of assuming where it is.
Takes one character from the start and one just after the space, using correct substring bounds.
Joins the letters and periods in the right order, and returns the result (does not print it).
Keeps the method header exactly as given.

codeTasks.title: Percent correct
codeTasks.header: public static double percentCorrect(int correct, int total)
codeTasks.does: Returns the exact percentage of correct answers, not rounded: percentCorrect(7, 8) returns 87.5.
rubric: Makes the division happen in double arithmetic (for example 100.0 * correct / total), so 7 of 8 gives 87.5, not 0.0 or 87.0.
Does not round or cast the result to int.
Returns the value (does not print it).
Keeps the method header exactly as given.
